author: Sooner State News
title: Oklahoma to receive $525,000 from Cash App settlement over fraud protections
text:
Oklahoma to receive $525,000 from Cash App settlement over fraud protections
Attorney General Gentner Drummond announced on July 15 that Oklahoma will receive nearly $525,000 as part of a $45 million multistate settlement with Block, Inc., the company behind Cash App. The agreement resolves allegations that Block misled consumers about the safety of its app, failed to protect users from fraud on the platform, and did not provide promised or legally required fraud protection and resolution.
“Cash App told Oklahomans their money was safe while fraud on the platform was climbing and the company did nothing to stop it,” Drummond said. “Companies that build a product around handling people's paychecks and benefits don't get to treat customer protection as optional. This settlement forces Block to actually deliver the safeguards it promised to the people who trusted it with their money.”
According to Drummond’s office, Block marketed Cash App as secure—implying bank-level protections that were not in place—while instances of fraud increased. The company also encouraged consumers without traditional bank accounts to use Cash App as their primary financial account. Minimal identity checks at sign-up allowed scammers easy access; lack of phone support for years left users vulnerable to fake support lines operated by scammers; and a promotional campaign called "Cash App Fridays" led users to publicly post account IDs, which were exploited by scammers posing as Cash App representatives.
As a result of these practices, some users found themselves locked out of their funds for weeks with no way to recover stolen money. Under terms of the settlement, Block must now provide live daily customer support, cease misleading safety claims and marketing tactics linked to fraud such as “Cash App Fridays,” educate users about common scams, investigate complaints thoroughly, and reimburse valid claims in accordance with legal requirements.
The Oklahoma Attorney General focuses on combating crime—including organized crime through collaboration with state and federal partners—ensuring government transparency, strengthening tribal relations, upholding public legal services within Oklahoma operations, advocating for policies supporting energy and education sectors, and pursuing tougher laws against crimes such as rape and drug distribution, according to the official biography.
